sources.entry: xbar - Put the output from any script or program into your macOS Menu Bar.

summary.one_liner: xbar is a macOS menu bar app that displays the output of any script or program as a menu bar item, rewritten in Go as a successor to BitBar.
summary.what_it_does: xbar puts the output from any script or program into the macOS menu bar. It is described as a complete rewrite from the ground up, written in Go by @matryer and @leaanthony using Wails.app. Plugins are managed from within the app via Preferences > Plugins, where users can discover and install them from an online plugin repository. Plugins live in a folder at ~/Library/Application Support/xbar/plugins. The README says existing BitBar plugins can be moved into that folder to work with xbar. Writing your own plugins is covered by a separate guide linked from the README.
use_cases: show script output in the macOS menu bar
monitor system status from the menu bar
install and manage menu bar plugins
migrate BitBar plugins to a new app
how_to_run: Download the latest release of xbar.
Open xbar from the menu bar and choose Preferences > Plugins... to discover and manage plugins.
Place plugin scripts in ~/Library/Application Support/xbar/plugins to install them manually.
notable: Successor to BitBar, rewritten from the ground up in Go
Built with Wails.app for desktop apps using Go and web frontend tech
Plugin browsing and management inside the app
BitBar plugins can be moved into the new plugin folder
caveats: The README says pull requests are not accepted; contributions should start as issues
